source.title: Quantifying the Impact of Label Noise on Federated Learning
source.authors: Shu-Qi Ke; Chao Huang; Xin Liu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures how injected label noise affects generalization and convergence in federated learning, a new setting relative to the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study tests label-noise effects on global-model test accuracy, convergence, and overfitting. Its path-norm results measure path-norm growth across rounds and architectures/algorithms, not whether path-norm ranks train–test gaps as in V7. No result tests the listed memorization, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, width, or memorized-example-removal claims.
record.test_reason: The study measures label-noise effects and path-norm growth in federated learning, but none of V1–V8. It does not measure random-label fitting alongside natural-label generalization, and path-norm growth does not test magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking of generalization gaps. The record's T3 classification is therefore incorrect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors report approximately linear, sometimes piecewise linear, accuracy degradation with label noise, slower convergence, and greater overfitting. They derive a noise-linear upper bound under stated assumptions, with a path-norm specialization, and acknowledge that the bound can be loose.
record.recipe_differences: Studies federated learning with client-partitioned data and deliberately injected label noise; evaluates global-model accuracy, training convergence, and path-norm evolution rather than the listed standard-training generalization interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured effects vary with label-noise proportion and communication round; test accuracy is reported across FedAvg, SCAFFOLD, and FedNova, with algorithm rankings depending on noise level in the paper's summary.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing label noise generally reduces global-model test accuracy, slows local training-loss convergence, and increases overfitting in the tested federated settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Federated learning performance depends on client label noise, with approximately linear or piecewise linear accuracy declines and slower convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Path-norm proxy increases during federated training and differs in scale across algorithms and network depths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Federated ReLU networks exhibit path-norm growth consistent with the paper's polynomial upper bound.

record.problems: The authors say the generalization upper bound can be loose and describe experiments as using a small number of clients. Several accuracy and loss results are plotted without exact values in the text. The 30-client figure caption's noise percentages do not match the prose's stated error-ratio range.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported result families were left out. Figures 8–14 show additional individual plotted values, but exact values are not stated in the text and were not reconstructed from plots.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels, natural-label held-out performance under the same recipe, and chance held-out performance with random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, small-data exceptions, excessive dropout, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and comparisons with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures do not establish those effects; this does not dispute the reported noise or path-norm findings. No omitted result in the supplied text bears on a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization coexisting with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance.
Large versus small batch generalization under epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking of train–test gaps.
Effect of removing memorized examples on test accuracy.

rows.operation_detail: Train on two equally sized client datasets with uniformly flipped labels at varying client-specific noise levels; report global-model test accuracy.

conditions.value: client noise levels varied over (wp1, wp2) ∈ {0%, 10%, 20%, . . . , 80%, 90%}2

rows.baseline: 0% label noise; exact value not stated in text
rows.value: Figure 8 reports the test-accuracy surface; exact values figure only. Linear regression has coefficient of determination R² = 0.98 (Figure 9).
rows.note: The paper states a negative bilinear relation and strong linear relation between test accuracy and label noise; the accuracy values themselves are shown in figures.
rows.check: The two-client pilot uses FedAvg only, not all three algorithms. R² = 0.98 describes the regression fit, not accuracy or random-label memorization. No training-fit result establishes V1.
